tasks.short: Distribute patient menus, collect diet sheets and deliver food

steps.what: Find the current menus and patient or nursing-unit distribution references
Check and distribute the applicable menus to hospital patients
Collect completed diet sheets and clarify missing patient or meal details
Check patient identifiers and diet-sheet completeness before food distribution
Match food trays and snacks to the checked patient or unit references
Check and deliver the food trays or snacks to the patient or nursing unit

tasks.design: Use a current-menu index in {DOCS} and the existing ward-reference view in {OTHER}, the hospital meal-distribution system. The worker distributes menus, collects the actual sheets, checks references and physically delivers food; no new diet-entry or delivery log is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the right current menu and ward reference can require separate searches.
tasks.enabler_now: A native current-service view can put existing references together.
tasks.still_hard: Missing diet details, patient moves and food matching require direct checking.
tasks.human_edge: The worker checks the actual food and receiving patient or nursing unit.
tasks.altitude: Slightly easier reference retrieval with unchanged patient-facing delivery.

reach.learn: Which incomplete diet sheets need clinical clarification

evidence.claim: A current-menu and ward-reference view may reduce retrieval time; the digest does not establish automated patient-menu distribution or food delivery.

assumptions: Boundary includes physical menu distribution, actual sheet collection, checks and food delivery. The task does not state that the worker rekeys diet sheets; no such record write or trailing delivery record is invented.

Menu staff produce the current menu, ward staff maintain patient/unit references and patients or assisting ward staff produce completed diet sheets through existing meal selection. The worker's collection, completeness checking and clarification time is fully retained in s3/s4; absent identifiers or conflicting instructions go to ward staff rather than an inferred diet rule.

OTHER is the hospital meal-distribution category. Native reference configuration removes only two of10 reference hours by avoiding duplicate searches. Templates do not replace collecting sheets, patient checks or carrying food.
External authority applies to direct patient delivery; delivery to nursing colleagues is internal. The handover check remains in s6 in either case, with no author-save approval.
unknowns: Whether current menu and ward references already appear together
Whether this worker performs any real diet-sheet rekeying today
research_questions: Can a current-service view remove a separate lookup without obscuring patient moves or diet-sheet discrepancies?

already_counted.description: Diet-sheet collection, completeness checks and tray matching remain in s3, s4 and s5.

incremental.description: Worker checks the current-service filter after menu-cycle changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact current menu, applicable patient and distribution period checked before physical handover; changed instructions require a renewed check.
Actual tray or snack, diet-sheet reference and current receiving patient/unit checked immediately before delivery; changed destination or food invalidates the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R98, gross2 less upkeep0.5 gives net1.5. Low0 retains the existing workflow when the current-service view is already available and no change is adopted. High0.75 retains8.75 reference hours where some ward references still need manual search, plus90 physical/clarification/checking hours: R98.75, net0.75. Central retains eight reference hours; no physical handling is reduced.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep records of food quantities used

steps.what: Observe, measure or count the quantities of food actually used
Write the food quantities used in the existing usage record
Check the recorded quantities and correct missing items or unit errors

tasks.design: Use a native food-use form in {OPS_SYSTEM} with current item references, service date defaults and explicit units. The worker still measures actual use, enters quantities and checks them; no recipe-based estimate substitutes for observed use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper usage records repeatedly require item names, dates and unit context.
tasks.enabler_now: A native station form can reuse stable context while preserving the actual measured quantity.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded issues, leftovers and unit changes need physical checking.
tasks.human_edge: The worker distinguishes food actually used from nominal recipe consumption.
tasks.altitude: Write existing food-use records with less repeated context entry.

reach.learn: Which unit or item ambiguities make usage records unreliable

evidence.claim: Apicbase maintains ingredient data flowing into recipe and menu records; this supports reusable item context, not measurement of actual daily food use.
The reduction in repeated usage-record entry is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: The food-use record is explicitly part of the task and is read by kitchen management. No additional daily report, waste-camera record or send is added.

The worker produces actual quantity and unit observations in s1 and captures item, quantity, unit and service date in s2. Kitchen administration maintains item references in existing work. All35 observation hours and38.5 actual entry hours remain; unknown units or items require manual entry and checking in s3.

Native configuration comes first. Reusable item/date/unit context removes16.5 of55 record-writing hours; actual quantity entry, correction and ordinary same-system saving remain without a self-gate or saving on the save itself.
No sensor, automatic stock decrement, total calculation, out-of-range alert or recipe-derived usage posting is implied.
unknowns: How much record-writing time is repeated context versus actual quantity entry
Whether the current usage form already applies these defaults
research_questions: Does a station-form trial shorten repeated context entry while preserving measured quantities and explicit units?

already_counted.description: Actual observation, quantity entry and record checking remain in all three steps.

incremental.description: Worker checks item and unit defaults after menu changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R83.5, gross16.5 less upkeep1 gives net15.5. Low3 retains51 of55 entry hours where most items or units vary and context must be rewritten, plus45 observation/checking hours: R96, net3. High10 retains44 entry hours for a partly stable item list, plus45 other hours: R89, net10. Central retains38.5 entry hours only when stable context constitutes the identified16.5-hour removable operation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep direct food handling and patient checks personal while simplifying real food-use records.
role.ambitious_version: A food preparation worker who keeps useful consumption evidence without losing attention to the actual food and patient delivery.
